title: Helix Insurance — Claims routing + redaction pipeline (field notes)
content:
Meeting 2025-11-02 — initial intake call with Helix (Ops + Platform + Security)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood Solutions Eng), Luis (Helix Platform), Nora (Helix SecOps), Priya (Helix Claims lead)

Objective: capture constraints for a pilot to power claims triage (customer chat + automated routing) while ensuring PII redaction and auditability for regulators. Helix wants a VPC/on‑prem connector initially, then a Dedicated pool if throughput warrants.

Top-level requirements (verbatim from call):
- Real-time triage: average 95th %-ile latency <= 350ms for 256‑token responses under steady 50 rps.
- PII redaction: all PHI/PII must be scrubbed from logs before leaving Helix network (no raw transcripts in Redwood hosted logs).
- Audit trail: immutable, queryable event stream showing model version, prompt hash, response redaction mask, and decision outcome for each claim.
- Fallback policy: if private capacity unavailable, failover to a sanitized hosted variant with stricter redact rules.
- Explainability: brief rationale snippet (1–2 sentences) attached to routed outcome for human review.

Constraints / gotchas surfaced on call:
- Helix telematics attachments (images) will be preprocessed by their pipeline; Redwood only needs to handle text summarization and entity redaction.
- Legal requires retention of audit metadata for 7 years; Helix cannot host audit stream in a location outside their control.
- They will insist on KMS integration (HSM-backed) for encryption keys.
- High variability in claim size: many requests small (~30 tokens) but occasional long legal narratives (~3–4k tokens). Need graceful truncation / chunking.
- Tokenization differences: Helix uses a custom prompt framing with templated customer metadata that must be preserved for routing rules but redacted for storage.

Initial technical approach notes (sketch):
- Private deployment with a thin Redwood control plane in Helix VPC (private-control, private-data). All raw user transcripts stay in the VPC; only redact+metadata exported via an encrypted audit export to Helix S3.
- Redaction flow: run a two‑stage prompt pipeline on dedicated model variant: 1) entity extraction (structured tags: name, SSN, policy#, DOB) -> local redaction map; 2) response generation using redacted prompt + produce "redaction_mask" list of byte ranges + canonicalized entities. Store only redaction_mask + canonicalized entities in audit log (no raw PII).
- Model variants: recommend quantized 8‑bit medium LLM (latency/cost sweet spot) for triage and use larger model only for complex long narratives (can be routed asynchronously).
- Batching policy: continuous batching preferred but with per‑tenant max latency = 250ms to preserve tail latency. Suggest initial batch window 10ms and max batch size 8.
- KV cache per tenant to accelerate repeated context for policy lookups; invalidate on policy changes.

Operational / observability considerations:
- Console: need per-route cost + tokens + redact error rate dashboards. Add a custom metric: redact_false_negative_rate (cases where audit review found unredacted PII).
- Tracing hooks: include request_id -> model_version -> redaction_mask in trace for SRE debugging.
- Canary plan: phased rollouts; start with 0.1% of production traffic in copy mode (responses not acted on), then 1%, then 10%. Helix legal wants a manual signoff before 1%->10%.

Security checklist items Helix demanded quickly:
- KMS/HSM integration: yes (show KMS key rotation timeline).
- No user data persisted in Redwood hosted logs: must ensure private deployment configuration and scrub logs at runtime.
- Access control: RBAC for Helix users + token scoping for routes.

Open questions (must clarify with Helix before next call):
1) Who signs off as legal approver for the redaction test set? Helix to provide contacts.
2) Which jurisdictions' PII rules govern retention (affects export location)?
3) Are there existing regex/NER rules Helix prefers we apply pre‑model? They mentioned an in-house SSN sanitizer.
4) Spike to confirm: how many concurrent claims processors do they expect peak? (Luis to share QPS forecast spreadsheet)

Quick POC tasks (owner, ETA):
- Seed 10k prompt set: Helix to share anonymized claim snippets (Luis) — due 2025-11-07.
- Small private deployment skeleton (Redwood infra): Maya/Evan to spin up dev VPC controller + sample route with redaction pipeline — due 2025-11-12.
- Redaction test harness: create unit tests to assert no PII in exported audit blobs (Evan) — due 2025-11-14.
- Canary run plan doc + legal signoff checklist (Maya, with Nora) — draft due 2025-11-10, final before 1% traffic.

Notes from quick feasibility spike (during call):
- Streaming vs non‑streaming: streaming complicates redaction because tokens emit as generated. Proposed approach: buffer generation until redaction pass completes then stream sanitized output; for UX-critical chat, emit high‑level intermediate placeholders like "[redacting sensitive info]" until final sanitized snippet available. Helix open to small initial latency bump.
- Audit export format: newline-delimited JSON with fields: request_id, ts, model_version, prompt_hash, redaction_mask (base64), canonical_entities, route_decision. Helix insists on gzip + server-side encrypt to their S3.

Next meeting: 2025-11-09 11:00 PT (technical deep dive + we will have initial skeleton infra demo).

Misc quick references / tickets: CLM-842 (requirements), INF-2197 (private-control work), PR #128 (ingest redaction helpers).

Notes to self: keep the POC narrow—start with text-only triage, block attachments until we have stable redaction masks. Emphasize clear rollback DSL in rollout plan so Helix legal feels comfortable.
